s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive orbital and facial syndrome with mass effect
key_facts: History of nodular sclerosing type stage IIE Hodgkin lymphoma
Treated with 4 cycles of ABVC and 3060 cGY radiation
Previous excisions of left upper eyelid mass
Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells on histopathology
Immunohistochemistry positive for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme
MRI shows lesion with marked interval enlargement within the orbit and extension through the frontal sinus into the intracranial compartment
Tumor centered at the left cavernous sinus and orbital apex involving the left intracavernous/supraclinoid segments of the internal carotid artery
Extension into the right cavernous sinus and right sphenoid sinus with mass effect on the left temporal lobe
Genetic testing shows splicing variant (c.2515-1G>A) in the PALB2 gene

shortlist.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
shortlist.why_kept: Multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, positive for CD68

shortlist.label: Erdheim-Chester disease
shortlist.why_kept: Histopathology and imaging findings consistent with this rare histiocytic disorder

shortlist.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, although immunohistochemistry profile is not typical

shortlist.label: Histiocytic sarcoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive clinical course and histopathological features of a malignant histiocytic neoplasm

shortlist.label: Giant cell tumor
shortlist.why_kept: Presence of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells, although clinical context and imaging findings are not typical

raw.rationale: The patient's presentation with a multinodular proliferation of osteoclast-like multinucleated giant cells and mononuclear cells, along with positive immunohistochemistry for CD68 and negative for CD45, S100, desmin, and lysozyme, is more consistent with Erdheim-Chester disease. The genetic testing showing a splicing variant in the PALB2 gene does not directly support Rosai-Dorfman disease.
raw.anchor_refutation: Rosai-Dorfman disease typically presents with lymphadenopathy and does not usually involve the orbit or have the specific immunohistochemical profile seen in this patient.

rejected.label: Rosai-Dorfman disease
rejected.why: Does not typically involve the orbit and has a different immunohistochemical profile

rejected.label: Langerhans cell histiocytosis
rejected.why: Typically has a different immunohistochemical profile, with positivity for S100 and CD1a

rejected.label: Histiocytic sarcoma
rejected.why: Usually presents with more aggressive features and a different clinical course

rejected.label: Giant cell tumor
rejected.why: Typically occurs in bone and has a distinct radiographic appearance
